content: The text provided is a detailed and technical description of various food items, their nutrient profiles, and their preparation forms. 1. Bread and Grain Products: Whole wheat bread, chapati, or roti are consumed in their natural form, with two servings of whole wheat bread being common. Corn-based bread is available in both leavened and unleavened forms, with one serving each. Paratha made from whole wheat is consumed in one serving, while sorghum-based bread is available in both leavened and unleavened forms, with one serving each. Maize tortillas are consumed in four servings, while fermented maize injera and millet injera are consumed in one serving each. Whole grain bread and rolls with wheat germ, multigrain, rye, spelt, or unspecified wheat are consumed in varying quantities, with eight servings of unspecified wheat being the highest. 2. Refined Grain Bakery Products: Refined flour chapati or roti is consumed in three servings, while paratha made from refined flour is consumed in one serving. Refined wheat flour tortillas are consumed in two servings, and white bread and rolls are consumed in 30 servings. 3. Starchy Roots, Tubers, and Plantains: Nutrient values are adjusted for raw items. Arrowroot and breadfruit are consumed raw in one serving each. Cassava, including white yam, is consumed raw in nine servings, while cassava flour (boiled or as dough) is consumed in two servings. Fermented cassava paste (fufu wet) and grated, toasted cassava (gari) are consumed in one serving each. Green banana flour is consumed raw in two servings, while cooked plantains, including green bananas, are consumed in eight servings. Boiled potatoes are consumed in 30 servings, while white sweet potatoes are consumed in 10 servings. Other starchy roots, tubers, and pulps are consumed in two servings, and taro is consumed cooked in one serving. 4. Vitamin A-Rich Fruits: Nutrient values are provided for raw forms unless otherwise indicated. Cooked or canned apricots are consumed in one serving, while raw apricots are consumed in five servings. Cantaloupe is consumed in two servings, lucuma fruit in one serving, and cooked or canned mango in two servings. Raw mango is consumed in 16 servings, papaya in 15 servings, and passion fruit in three servings. Japanese persimmons are consumed in two servings, tamarillo (tree tomato) in two servings. 5. Berries: Nutrient values are provided for raw forms unless otherwise indicated. Unspecified berries are consumed in three servings. Cooked or canned blackberries and blueberries are consumed in one serving each, while raw blackberries and blueberries are consumed in one and two servings, respectively. Currants (red or white) are consumed in one serving, raspberries (including black and red) in one serving, and cooked or canned strawberries in two servings. Raw strawberries are consumed in eight servings. 6. Citrus Fruits: Nutrient values are provided for raw forms. Citron (limon real) is consumed in one serving, unspecified citrus fruits in two servings, grapefruit in one serving, oranges in 22 servings, and tangerines in 10 servings. 7. Vitamin C-Rich Fruits: Guava is consumed in seven servings, jujube in one serving, kiwifruit in six servings, and lychee in one serving. 8. Bananas: Cooked or canned bananas are consumed in three servings, while raw bananas are consumed in 33 servings. 9. High-Fat Fruits: African pear (ube, eben) is consumed in one serving, avocado in nine servings, and coconut meat in four servings. 10. Other Fruits: Cooked or canned apples are consumed in five servings, while raw apples are consumed in 24 servings. Applesauce is consumed in five servings, casaba melon in one serving, cherries in four servings, and fresh figs in one serving. Grapes are consumed raw in 13 servings and cooked or canned in one serving. Japanese pears, mangosteen, naranjilla, and nectarines are consumed in one serving each. Cooked or canned peaches are consumed in two servings, while raw peaches are consumed in seven servings. Cooked or canned pears are consumed in three servings, while raw pears are consumed in 11 servings. Pineapple is consumed in five servings, plums in one serving, pomegranate in three servings, quinces in one serving, rambutan in one serving, rose apple in one serving, and watermelon in eight servings. 11. Dark Green Leafy Vegetables: Nutrient values are provided for boiled forms unless otherwise indicated. Amaranth leaves are consumed in five servings, bok choy in three servings, baobab leaves in one serving, and bean leaves in one serving. Chinese broccoli is consumed raw with retention adjustments in one serving. Cassava leaves are consumed in three servings, chard in four servings, and chrysanthemum leaves raw with retention adjustments in one serving. Cocoyam leaves, cowpea leaves, and other dark green leaves are consumed in varying quantities. 12. Other Brassicas: Broccoli, including broccoli rabe and Chinese broccoli, is consumed in 16 servings. Brussels sprouts are consumed in one serving, cauliflower in 12 servings, and green cabbage in 13 servings. 13. Vitamin A-Rich Orange Vegetables: Carrots are consumed in 27 servings, pumpkin flesh in 15 servings, yellow/orange sweet potatoes in 10 servings, and winter squash in eight servings. 14. Peppers and Tomatoes: Green bell peppers are consumed boiled in four servings and raw in three servings. Red bell peppers are consumed boiled in five servings, and yellow bell peppers are consumed raw in one serving. Cooked red tomatoes are consumed in 13 servings, while raw red tomatoes are consumed in 30 servings. 15. Legumes: Nutrient values are provided for raw or dry forms with retention adjustments. Adzuki beans are consumed in one serving, mature beans (unspecified type) in 14 servings, and small white beans in four servings. Black beans are consumed in four servings, broad beans in one serving, and chickpeas in five servings. 16. Nuts and Seeds: Roasted almonds and almond butter are consumed in three servings, roasted cashews in one serving, and hazelnuts in one serving. Pumpkin/squash seed kernels are consumed dried in one serving and roasted in one serving. 17. Animal Products: Beef liver is consumed braised in six servings, chicken liver simmered in six servings, and pig liver braised in five servings. Chicken (lower fat items) is consumed stewed or braised in 28 servings, while duckling is consumed braised in four servings. 18. Fish: Anchovies are consumed whole, dried, or smoked in four servings. Sardines (Atlantic, canned) are consumed in two servings, and mackerel (cooked) is consumed in three servings. 19. Fats and Oils: Butter is consumed in 13 servings, anhydrous butter (including ghee) in five servings, and coconut oil in two servings. Olive oil is consumed in six servings, and soybean oil is consumed in 19 servings. 20. Single Staple Food Patterns: Nutrient profiles for rice-based patterns are modeled using white, long-grain, unenriched rice in its raw form. Maize-based patterns are modeled using whole-grain white corn flour typical in African settings. Root and tuber-based patterns are modeled using nutrient profiles for cooked forms of roots, tubers, and plantains.
